text:
maria: heads-up — eu-west1 saw a wave of model-serving restarts over the last 30m. lots of evictions and reschedules, cost spiked because many fell back to on-demand pools.
kevin: +1. pattern looks like QoS 'islanding' — nodes with mixed GPU types ended up isolated due to strict topologySpread + pod affinity. scheduler kept attempting exact cohort binds and failed.
nash: we also had transient rack-level network flaps around the same time, nodes Tainted:NetworkUnreachable for ~40s which caused kubelet to set pods to BestEffort? saw multiple Kubelet evict events.
liz: scheduler logs show repeated rebind/preempt loops. relevant lines: 
```
I0304 10:22:49.123 scheduler.go:551] binding pod model-serving-abc to node-gpu-12 attempt=3 reason=InsufficientGPU
I0304 10:22:50.321 scheduler.go:612] preempting pod trainer-batch-5 to make room
I0304 10:22:51.987 scheduler.go:640] requeue pod model-serving-abc due to topologySpread conflict
```
maria: autoscaler launched 4 on-demand nodes to satisfy immediate demand (autoscaler-bot posted). that fixed latency but cost jumped.
autoscaler-bot: launched instance-group eu-west1-on-demand-3 (4 nodes) due to unschedulable pods count > 25.
kevin: posted the quick query output — majority of unschedulable had nodeAffinity: preferredDuringScheduling weight 100 and topologySpread constraints pinned to gpu-cohort label. so scheduler prioritized placement into exact cohorts instead of soft packing.
nash: kubectl snippet for the most-hit pod: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: model-serving-abc
spec:
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        podAffinityTerm:
          topologyKey: "gpu-cohort"
```
kevin: proposed mitigations: lower preferred weight to 50, add soft-affinity fallback, and reduce topologySpread strictness. also add scheduler scoring tweak to favor packing over exact-cohort matches when freeGPU < X.
tom: short-term ops: cordon the flaky rack nodes, patch eviction-throttle on kubelet (--eviction-hard/soft tweak), and add a defrag job to attempt binpacking of evictable BestEffort trainer pods during maintenance window.
liz: long-term: we should implement a defragmentation controller that looks for scatter islands and schedules a controlled draining + best-effort migration during low traffic. also expose a placement hint to model-serving so it can gracefully reduce concurrency before being evicted.
maria: telemetry note — we lost cohort label heartbeat in metrics so it's hard to correlate. we need an event emitter that tags evictions with scheduling decision id.
kevin: small ergonomics: add metric reporting for 'topologySpread failures' and 'preferred affinity weight hits' to the console and alert when > 5/min.
nash: experiment idea — introduce a soft 'pack-score' plugin that penalizes node spread when it increases GPU fragmentation by > 1 free-card. can we prototype in next scheduler build?
liz: worked offline with infra — immediate rollout: reduce affinity weight to 60, cordon 3 nodes in rack-7, and temp lower topologySpread enforcement. will monitor for 1h.
maria: thanks. I'll also open a short-runbook for on-call: how to detect QoS islanding, commands to cordon/drain, and the preflight check for the defrag job.
sre-bot: runbook created: https://internal/redwood/runbooks/qos-islanding (created by maria) :thumbsup:
kevin: follow-up action items: (1) telemetry patch (maria), (2) scheduler scoring PR (kevin), (3) defrag controller RFC (liz). tagging owners.
maria: closing the loop — no further evictions after autoscaler nodes stabilized + temporary changes. keeping watch for 2h and will revert cordon after that.
